title: Patterns and the Fibonacci sequence
examples: Teacher, how do I find the next number in this pattern?
Where do we see this Fibonacci pattern in the real world?
Is the Fibonacci sequence always about spirals?

explain.say: Today we are looking at number patterns called the Fibonacci sequence.
To find the next number you add the two numbers before it together.

draw.text: Next number = Sum of previous two

explain.say: Let us try to find the next three numbers in the sequence together.
The pattern continues because you always add the last two numbers.
This pattern shows up in the spirals of things in nature around us.
Look at a sunflower head it has seeds arranged in perfect spirals.

faq.q: Does this pattern only work for numbers?
faq.a: No it can describe patterns in many things not just numbers. It can describe the spirals of seeds or petals.
asks: Is it only for counting things?

faq.q: What is the golden ratio and how is it related?
faq.a: The golden ratio is a special number that shows up when you look at the ratio of numbers far apart in the sequence. It is approximately one point six one eight.
asks: What is the special number here?
Does it relate to the golden spiral?

faq.q: If I start with different numbers will it still work?
faq.a: The basic rule is always adding the two previous numbers. If you change the start, the pattern changes too.
asks: Can I change the first two numbers?
Does the rule change if I start differently?

faq.q: Why do these spirals look so perfect?
faq.a: Nature uses this pattern because it is the most efficient way to pack seeds or petals tightly. It leaves no wasted space.
asks: Is it an accident in nature?
Why is this arrangement so good?

faq.q: What is the difference between this and just counting?
faq.a: Counting is just listing numbers in order. The Fibonacci sequence has a specific rule about adding the two numbers before it.
asks: What makes it different from counting?

facts: Each number is the sum of the two preceding ones.
This pattern appears in the arrangement of petals on flowers.
The ratio between consecutive numbers approaches the golden ratio.

quiz.say: What is the next number after 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8?
quiz.why: You must add the last two numbers, which are five and eight, to get thirteen.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you are only adding the two numbers before the last one.
wrong.1: This is too far ahead; you must find the number right after eight first.
wrong.3: This is a common mistake because you might only add the last number to the one before it.

quiz.say: If the sequence starts with 2 and 3, what is the third number?
quiz.why: The rule is to add the two numbers before it, so two plus three equals five.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you are adding the first number twice.
wrong.2: This is too large; you must only add the two numbers given.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because you must use the addition rule on the two previous numbers.

quiz.say: Which real-life object often shows this spiral pattern?
quiz.why: Pinecones and sunflower seeds use this pattern because it is efficient for packing.

wrong.0: Windows are usually straight lines, not spirals.
wrong.1: Roads follow paths, not the Fibonacci spiral.
wrong.2: While circles are round, the specific seed arrangement is different.
